title: ROLE_REQUEST: a Dell writes in for a role (NFRA_CTLPLN PRD v0.8 C-ROLE-REQUEST (a)), and the laptop's separate answer
description: Two documents, two writers, two files. The REQUEST is written by the Dell that needs a role, at org/devices/role_requests/<device>/<request_id>.json (a per-box directory: only that box writes there). The ANSWER is written by the laptop, later, at org/devices/role_requests/<laptop device>/answers/<request_id>.json; the laptop never edits a Dell's record. A request's EFFECTIVE status is its answer's `status` when an answer file exists, else `requested`: `status` is the field a reader rejects on. A Dell never creates, edits or attaches policy to a role; it asks, and each permission it asks for is tied to the code line that needs it. Writer, validator and lister: org/devices/role_request.py. The verbs that write an answer (mark-applied, mark-refused) are the laptop's, in the same file; they refuse unless AGENTBUS_DEVICE names the control-plane box. The round trip a Dell runs: org/devices/role_roundtrip_check.py.

device.description: the register name of the box writing in (its AGENTBUS_DEVICE)

tailnet_name.description: that box's tailnet name, from the register

requested_by.description: the serial of the seat that wrote the request

project.description: the project code the work is placed under

terraform_root.description: a directory under infra/aws/terraform/ where the laptop writes the role

action.description: never an iam: action, never a bare *; the writer and the validator refuse both

code_ref.description: <repo path>:<line> of the code line that needs this permission; the file and the line must exist

status.description: always requested in the Dell's record; the effective status comes from the answer file
